description: Manage your BambooHR employee records, time off, and reports: look people up, keep their details current, and see who is out.

bamboohr_employee_terminated_trigger.description: Beta. Runs once when a termination is entered on an employee's BambooHR record, which is often before their last day, with their name, job, work email, last day and their manager's name and work email, for an offboarding checklist with no lookups. The last day is often weeks away when it runs, so a step that cuts off access straight away (suspending an account) locks out someone who is still working: say so, or leave that to IT on the day. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.display_name: Their name as BambooHR shows it.
output.employee_id: The employee's BambooHR id, for later BambooHR steps.
output.employment_status: Their employment status as BambooHR records it, such as Terminated.
output.manager_email: Their manager's work email, to send the offboarding checklist to. Blank when they have no manager.
output.manager_name: Their manager's name. Blank when they have no manager.
output.termination_date_display: Their last day written for a message, such as Nov 30, 2026, so no step has to format it.
output.work_email: Their work email address, such as ada@example.com (the account to suspend).

bamboohr_employee_updated_trigger.description: Runs each time an employee's BambooHR record changes, such as a new job title, department or manager, with their details as they are now. Several changes between checks start one run. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.changed_at: When the record was last changed (UTC).
output.display_name: Their name as BambooHR shows it.
output.employee_id: The employee's BambooHR id, for later BambooHR steps.
output.hire_date_display: Beta. Their hire date written for a message, such as Nov 2, 2026, so no step has to format it.

bamboohr_new_employee_trigger.description: Runs for each employee added to BambooHR, with their name, job title, department, work email and hire date. Beta: each run also has their personal email and their manager's name and work email, so a workflow can welcome them and tell their manager without looking anyone up. Employees already there when the workflow is turned on don't start it. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.changed_at: When the record was last changed (UTC).
output.display_name: Their name as BambooHR shows it.
output.employee_id: The employee's BambooHR id, for later BambooHR steps.
output.hire_date_display: Beta. Their hire date written for a message, such as Nov 2, 2026, so no step has to format it.
output.manager_email: Beta. Their manager's work email address, such as grace@example.com, ready to send a message to or to look the manager up in Slack. Blank when they have no manager.
output.manager_name: Beta. The name of their manager (who they report to in BambooHR), such as Grace Hopper. Blank when they have no manager.
output.personal_email: Beta. Their personal (home) email address, such as ada.lovelace@gmail.com, to welcome them before their work email works. Blank when BambooHR has none for them or the API key may not read it.
output.supervisor: Who they report to, as BambooHR writes it. For a message, use 'manager_name'.

bamboohr_time_off_requested_trigger.description: Runs for each new BambooHR time off request waiting for a decision, with who asked, the kind of time off and the dates, for one kind or all of them. Beta: each run also has the employee's work email, their manager's name and work email (to ask the manager to approve), how many days the request is, and the dates written out for a message. Requests already there when the workflow is turned on don't start it. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.amount: How much time off, in the unit below. For a length in days whatever the unit, use 'days'.
output.dates_display: Beta. Both dates in one phrase for a message or a calendar event's title, such as Dec 22, 2026 to Jan 2, 2027 (or just Dec 22, 2026 for a single day), so no step has to format them.
output.days: Beta. How many days off the request is, as a number such as 4 or 0.5, whether BambooHR counts this kind of time off in days or hours. Compare this, not 'amount', to ask whether a request is longer than so many days. For a kind counted in hours it is the number of days with any time booked, so a part day counts as one day; when BambooHR doesn't list the days, it is the hours divided by 8.
output.employee_email: Beta. The work email address of the employee who asked, such as ada@example.com. Blank when BambooHR has none for them.
output.employee_id: The BambooHR id of the employee who asked.
output.employee_name: The name of the employee who asked.
output.employee_note: The note the employee left, if any.
output.end_date: The last day off, such as 2027-01-02.
output.end_date_display: Beta. The last day off written for a message, such as Jan 2, 2027.
output.manager_email: Beta. Their manager's work email address, such as grace@example.com, ready to use as the person asked by an Ask a person step. Blank when they have no manager.
output.manager_name: Beta. The name of the employee's manager (who they report to in BambooHR), such as Grace Hopper. Blank when they have no manager.
output.request_id: The request's id, for Update a time off request's status.
output.requested_on: The day the request was made.
output.start_date: The first day off, such as 2026-12-21.
output.start_date_display: Beta. The first day off written for a message, such as Dec 22, 2026.
output.time_off_type: The kind of time off, such as Vacation.

parameters.description: Only watch requests for this kind of time off: pick one, or type its name, such as Vacation. Leave empty to watch them all.
parameters.name: time_off_type
